title: release: after a stable publish, a `next` dist-tag already on a stable version is left below `latest` — `npx create-objectstack@next` scaffolds 18.5.0 after 18.6.0
body:
qa#1 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYpxQpmErd1ixfkgbYh

Found by the post-release npm smoke #35181, as an off-clause probe beside cell F1b.

## What happens
`npm view create-objectstack dist-tags` → `{latest: '18.6.0', next: '18.5.0'}`. The same holds for `@objectstack/cli`, `spec`, `runtime`, `console` and `plugin-auth`. `npm view create-objectstack@next version` → 18.5.0.

## Mechanism (from the runner's reading of the script; the 18.6.0 release step log was not read)
- `release.yml`'s step "Move stale pre-release dist-tags up to latest" runs `scripts/release-dist-tags.mjs --apply`, with `continue-on-error`.
- The script leaves alone any tag that sits on a STABLE version, treating it as "a maintenance line".
- 18.5.0's sweep moved `next` onto the stable 18.5.0. From then on `next` looks like a pinned stable line, and the 18.6.0 sweep skipped it.

## Expected
Per #25581, `next` never resolves below `latest` after a stable publish. Treat `next` as a channel tag whose stable value below `latest` also moves. Read the 18.6.0 release step's log for a skip or a warning. The tag itself needs a one-time move, a maintainer-run registry action as in #25764.

Related, all closed: #25581, #25764, #26196, #30591.
